purpose: One pinned SPIDERMAN boundary: SPIDERMAN (Louden & Kreidberg 2018) owns spherical-harmonic brightness maps and the phase curves they produce, as published fits used them. cssEarth owns the paper transcription, the conversion to brightness temperature and scientific qualification.
license: spiderman-package is copyright 2016 Tom Louden under the MIT license of its repository (SPIDERMAN-LICENSE.txt, from github.com/tomlouden/SPIDERMAN at commit 379a5b6); the PyPI sdist carries no license file and its setup.py metadata says GNU GPLv3. batman-package is GPL-3.0 (BATMAN-NOTICE.txt). NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib and Astropy are BSD-style.
why: spiderman-package 1.0.3 (PyPI, 2019-09-11) is the last release. It builds only against the NumPy 1.x C API and old setuptools (setup.py imports numpy.distutils and passes its license as a list), so it has its own environment rather than the astroquery toolchain's Python 3.12 and NumPy 2.
importShim: spiderman/plot.py imports matplotlib._png, removed in Matplotlib 3.3, for its logo art. The runner registers an empty matplotlib._png module whose read_png raises before importing spiderman; no plotting function is called, so no SPIDERMAN code is changed or bypassed. HOME is an empty directory so no ~/.spidermanrc is read.
